The spec is unusually mature — the internal plan review already caught and fixed the three issues I would have raised first (whole-row vs. delta judgment, dual merge-base resolvers, TBD marker parity). My findings are refinements on the remaining seams:

findings.finding: Trailing blank lines left after the dead-comment removal (fixed in a follow-up edit: file trimmed to a single terminating newline, 1085 lines).
The on-trunk rule is re-derived locally rather than shared with git_helpers._iterate_changed_paths's identical derivation.
Comment for the redundant-conjunct fix was written in the register of the deletion rather than stating the invariant.
Still O(rows x document) parsing per spec file; pre-existing, advisory-path only.

Claim under doubt: the gate 'fails CLOSED on any git infrastructure gap' (fr_hygiene.py module docstring), so an unresolvable merge-base or a failed range diff can never green it — The fail-closed branches are downstream of an early return that cannot reach them. _iterate_changed_paths silently degrades to the single-commit view when the merge-base can't be resolved or the range diff fails, and the old 'not specs' early return fired before the merge-base fail-closed check ever ran.
findings.suggestion: Resolve base_sha BEFORE deciding 'no spec touched', or have the gate compute its own git diff base..commit rather than consuming a helper documented to degrade.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the new base_sha == head_sha branch only fires for a commit that is genuinely 'already contained in the trunk', so the SKIP is honest and the gate stays non-dodgeable — _branch_base_commit's candidates include local main/master; a commit made directly on the local trunk (not yet pushed) can make merge-base(main, commit) == commit, falsely reporting 'already on the trunk'.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish 'contained in origin's trunk' from 'base collapsed to HEAD because the local trunk branch points here'.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: 'N spec(s) touched, all edited FR row(s) clean' is a true statement about every FR row the run added or edited — _row_map called read_fr_rows without a rejects accumulator, so a row with a non-canonical id (e.g. hand-typed FR-1.02) is silently invisible to the gate and never judged.
findings.suggestion: Pass a rejects list into read_fr_rows for the HEAD text and fail closed (or name them in the detail) when a touched spec.md yields rows the reader declined.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: 'this FR's acceptance criteria' means the same thing on both halves of the decision — selecting touched rows and judging them — _touched_ids selected via _layer_coverage_ac.criteria_digests (region-scoped to a recognised '## Acceptance Criteria' section) while _row_findings judged via fr_criteria.criteria_for (whole-document) — a scope mismatch that could hide a criterion anchored outside the recognised region.
findings.suggestion: Use one reader for both halves.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the new cross-plugin parity test makes I8's dependence on /shipwright-adopt's TBD literal safe, and spec_document.py 'emits a literal TBD line for any FR it could not derive acceptance criteria for' — spec_document.py's TBD emission is conditional on has_any_ac; when NO feature yielded criteria (the common freshly-adopted, wholly-TBD shape), a different branch renders prose with no per-FR heading and no marker at all, so I8 is structurally incapable of firing on exactly that shape. The parity test only pins the constant, not the contract.
findings.suggestion: Make the parity test behavioral: render a spec via spec_document with a mixed and an all-empty AC set, and assert the marker appears under an FR heading.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: promoting I1/I2 from advisory to blocking for touched rows only changes 'what happens on a hit', so the deferred allowlist follow-up carries no shipped exposure — fr_hygiene_detectors._PASCAL_RE matches ordinary product vocabulary not in _NOT_SYMBOLS (LinkedIn, WhatsApp, TikTok, PowerPoint, OneDrive, SharePoint, QuickBooks, MailChimp, MongoDB), so a genuinely clean row can STOP F11 with no allowlist, no ack path, and no way for a consumer repo to extend _NOT_SYMBOLS.
findings.suggestion: Ship a minimal escape hatch (per-project allowlist or an acknowledgement key), or narrow the blocking subset to unambiguous detectors and leave the Pascal/camel heuristic advisory.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a wedged or stalled git degrades this gate to a reported failure rather than hanging F11 — spec_text_at's underlying _run_git calls carry no timeout (three per touched spec), and _branch_base_commit used to be resolved twice per invocation.
findings.suggestion: Pass an explicit timeout through spec_text_at's _run_git calls; avoid the duplicate merge-base resolution.

findings.finding: git blame` without a rev blames the working-tree file. An uncommitted (or just-modified) TBD line is attributed to the "Not Committed Yet" pseudo-commit, whose porcelain `committer-time` is `0` — so `age_days = (now - 0) // 86400` is ~20,000 days and a brand-new, never-committed TBD is reported as stale. The spec explicitly scopes I8 to a placeholder "committed for at least 90 days"; this path reports uncommitted ones.
findings.suggestion: either blame the pinned `HEAD` (`git blame HEAD -- path`) so uncommitted lines fail blame resolution and are skipped, or detect the all-zero commit sha in the porcelain header and return `None`.

findings.finding: The F11 gate suite never covers a spec.md that is newly added by the run (absent at the merge-base) nor a newly added criteria section under an existing row. The gate's behavior there depends entirely on whether `spec_text_at(base_sha, path)` returns `""` or `None` for a file that doesn't exist at the base — if it returns `None`, every new spec file fails finalization with "could not read … at the base commit", which would be a false-block regression the tests would not catch.
findings.suggestion: Add a real-git test where the run creates a brand-new `.shipwright/planning/02-x/spec.md` (clean content) and asserts the gate passes; this pins the absent-at-base semantics.

findings.finding: "Touched" is defined by comparing `(row.name, row.text)`. If `FrTableRow.text` is the full physical row line (rather than just the Description cell), then any cell edit — Priority, Basis, Layers, or a column reorder — marks the row touched and subjects a legacy dirty row to blocking I1/I2/I7. The spec's definition of touched is "Name/Description cells changed OR criteria digest changed"; a Priority-only edit on a legacy dirty row would block, contradicting the diff's own design note that regeneration/reflow must not mark every row touched. The visible tests cannot distinguish the two semantics (their edits always change the description too).
findings.suggestion: Confirm `row.text` is exactly the Description cell (or switch to `row.description`), and add a test that edits only a non-Description cell (e.g., Priority) of a legacy dirty row and asserts the gate does not fire.

findings.finding: The greenfield test asserts I7/I8 `status == "pass"` and `"no FR" in findings["I7"].detail`, but does not assert I8's detail content shape on a no-TBD spec (the analogous `"no FR"` check is made only against I7). A regression that silently empties I8's pass detail would pass this test.
findings.suggestion: Add `assert "no FR" in findings["I8"].detail` (or the exact empty-message) to the clean-fixture assertion block.

findings.finding: A TBD marker line appearing inside the FR table (e.g., a description cell containing the literal marker text) is attributed to the FR heading above it — whichever requirement's criteria section was last — producing a wrong-FR stale report. Low impact given the marker is machine-emitted, but the mapping is by physical proximity, not section ownership.
findings.suggestion: Restrict TBD scanning to lines between an FR heading and its criteria bullets (or skip lines beginning with `|`), so table cells can't be mis-attributed.  No security issues: the `git blame` subprocess call is list-argv with the path placed after `--`, so option injection is blocked; no secrets or untrusted sinks introduced. The detector-vocabulary move is a faithful copy (regexes identical, ReDoS-safe forms preserved) and the delegator preserves the public API, so no caller regression is visible. Spec acceptance criteria 1–7 are all implemented and covered by real-git tests, which are behavioral (assert failure/pass and row IDs), not vacuous.  Overall: solid, well-tested implementation of the spec; ship after fixing the uncommitted-TBD blame-age false positive and pinning the absent-at-base / description-cell semantics with a test.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: A newly added `spec.md` has no base-side file, so `spec_text_at(...base...)` returns `None` and the gate fails closed instead of comparing an empty catalogue to HEAD. A clean newly added spec is therefore rejected, while a dirty one is rejected without naming its FR or violation kind.
findings.suggestion: Treat a base-side missing path for an added spec as `""`; keep HEAD-side read failures blocking.

findings.finding: I8 flags any stale TBD marker without checking whether the FR also has real acceptance criteria. This contradicts the stated “I8 never fires on a row with real criteria” behavior; the existing test only tests a row with no TBD marker, so it misses the coexistence case.
findings.suggestion: Skip a TBD marker when that FR has one or more real criteria, and add a fixture containing both the marker and a valid criterion.

findings.finding: _blame_epoch` documents that subprocess failures return `None`, but it does not catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. A slow or stalled `git blame` can crash the entire compliance audit rather than leaving I8 advisory.
findings.suggestion: Catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` alongside the existing exceptions and return `None`.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The added-spec gate path and I8’s real-criteria handling violate intended behavior; the blame timeout path also makes the audit unexpectedly fragile. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
